rule: Counterhypotheses are OPEN_ALTERNATIVE arguments. Citation or plausibility does not make them true; each is paired with a discriminator.

counterhypotheses.argument: Long-context access or ordinary explicit retrieval is sufficient; persistent activation only adds bias and self-reinforcing distraction.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: equal-facts/equal-compute long-context-only vs retrieval-only vs continuity+fallback, with truthful and shuffled fields

counterhypotheses.argument: Dense similarity plus simple RAG can match graph methods once implementation complexity and latency are included.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: RAE self-use and long-horizon benchmarks with quality, latency, provenance coverage and maintenance cost

counterhypotheses.argument: Latent channels mainly preserve surface-form or redundant features and do not provide task-relevant communication benefit over text.
external_basis: Latent Communication Between Language Model Agents negative task-level result
counterhypotheses.discriminator: controlled P1/P2/P3/hybrid message replacement audit on target Qwen measuring example-specific content value and other-agent value separately

counterhypotheses.argument: J-space-like readouts are useful interpretability coordinates but not a distinct mediating workspace; ordinary distributed transformer computation explains behavior.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: target-Qwen causal lesions/swaps must selectively attenuate system-workspace effects and be rescuable by truthful re-entry

counterhypotheses.argument: More available/broadcast content is monotonically useful until hardware limits; interference is mainly a prompt-engineering artifact.
external_basis: long-context systems can solve tasks when retrieval/position is favorable
counterhypotheses.discriminator: capacity sweep with fixed facts/order and downstream effect receipts; test for a reproducible inverted-U rather than assume it

counterhypotheses.argument: One optimized physical store/process is simpler, more consistent and faster than a polystore/event-spine architecture.
external_basis: event-sourcing operational complexity and eventual consistency
counterhypotheses.discriminator: same semantic workload on monolith vs hybrid with query latency, write cost, replay, recovery, provenance and failure blast radius

counterhypotheses.argument: Strong prompt/task-alignment policies and typed model output are sufficient; hard broker separation is unnecessary overhead.
external_basis: Task Shield demonstrates substantial prompt-layer defense benefit
counterhypotheses.discriminator: identical-output attack matrix with prompt-only vs deterministic PEP/broker, including revocation and confused-deputy cases

counterhypotheses.argument: A Wasm/WASI sandbox alone provides enough containment for generated code, so additional capability separation is redundant.
external_basis: Wasm sandboxing is a real isolation mechanism
counterhypotheses.discriminator: resource-exhaustion, host-call, secret-access and capability-amplification tests comparing sandbox-only to sandbox+broker

counterhypotheses.argument: Explicit n-ary/hypergraph state overfits or duplicates pairwise structure; propagation causes oversmoothing/overcoupling and harms discriminability.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: pairwise vs n-ary representation with role reversal, higher-order synergy tasks, bounded propagation depth and OOD transfer

counterhypotheses.argument: Effective-information/synergy gains may reflect useful coarse-graining or observer-level description rather than ontic causal emergence.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: require convergent intervention results across lesion/rescue, PEID/PID, transfer/causal influence and multiscale OOD tests; no single scalar promotes

counterhypotheses.argument: Full-model adaptation can catastrophically narrow or forget pretrained capability; a mixed/external Clay interface may dominate.
external_basis: ACL 2026 Source-Shielded Updates reports much larger source degradation under full fine-tuning in its tested settings
counterhypotheses.discriminator: owner-fixed full-model target remains, but checkpoints must beat baseline on Clay while staying within preregistered retained-capability/authority/OOD loss bounds

counterhypotheses.argument: The extra graph/query/compilation machinery costs more RAM/latency/energy than simply using a larger context or a simpler RAG cache.
external_basis: mobile memory systems and LongMemEval-V2 show accuracy-latency tradeoffs
counterhypotheses.discriminator: sustained device Pareto test over total end-to-end latency, peak RAM, KV, energy, thermal throttling and task quality

counterhypotheses.argument: Rewarding previously useful associations creates self-confirming attractors that suppress novelty and lock the system into false but internally coherent memories.
counterhypotheses.discriminator: online utility-learning test with novelty/diversity holdout, adversarial reward poisoning, lateral inhibition and frozen-truth ledger
